description: Build a slick website mock-up of the self-building robot plan (voice-fc9b0f77 and all its replies: two-armed legless robot whose only job is to build itself; handheld-gripper bootstrap where humans build it using only the gripper; needle-nose-pliers-style small gripper; eye-level stereo cameras; servo-current force; start line = bought actuators, screws, electronics + 3D-printed parts, then push the line down toward raw materials and eventually mining, with chips bought; printers that build printers; iron, ferrite and Halbach or magnet-free motors; ship a built robot plus a kit that it assembles at the customer's home; robots building bigger or smaller robots one size step at a time; penny-doubling growth). Jake: 'Make a slick mock-up of that plan, the robot that could build itself. It should be a website, just locally hosted for now, but really really clean and modern looking. Very simple, and with a lot of graphics that you make of the robot.' Do: a simple, modern single-page site (e.g. plain HTML/CSS/JS or a minimal static build) in this repo; make lots of original robot illustrations (SVG and/or three.js renders of the legless two-armed robot, the pliers gripper, the robot assembling its sibling, the replication ladder, the doubling curve). Serve it on localhost (give the URL and a start command), and attach a screenshot as the pebble visual so Jake can see it without opening anything.

results.identified_issue: Static site in sites/self_building_robot (no framework, deliberately: local-only mock-up). All art is generated by robot.js: robot({x,y,s,L,R,head,left,right,cls}) with arm angles [upper, fore, gripper, jaw-open] in SVG degrees; pliers() is shared by every gripper so the design stays consistent. Hero uses requestAnimationFrame; #still or prefers-reduced-motion freezes it (screenshots use #still). Hero min-height is clamped to 820px because headless screenshots with tall windows blow up vh. Mobile only spot-checked in headless Chrome, which may enforce a min window width; a real-phone check is worth doing. Server is python3 http.server on 127.0.0.1:8790 started with nohup in this session; it won't survive a reboot.
results.summary: Built the self-building robot website: one clean page with 10 robot illustrations drawn in code, running at http://localhost:8790.
results.detailed_description:
It's running now at http://localhost:8790. To start it again later, run sites/self_building_robot/serve.sh. The screenshot above shows the top of the page and three of the illustrations.

It's one scrolling page, plain HTML, CSS and JS with no build step, in sites/self_building_robot/. Light, mostly white, with one orange accent and big headlines. All the art is SVG drawn by one small script from a single robot model, so every robot on the page is the same design in a different pose and size. In page order:
- Hero: the legless two-armed robot on its weighted base, with stereo eyes and pliers grippers. Its arms move slowly.
- The bootstrap rule: the handheld gripper = the gripper on the robot's wrist.
- The needle-nose pliers gripper, with labels for the pads, V-notch, bit pocket and wire cutter.
- Eyes at eye level: a person wearing a stereo camera band beside the robot, eyes on the same dashed line.
- Force from motor current: a current trace that rises on contact.
- The robot fitting an arm onto a half-built sibling.
- Printers building printers: 1, 2, 4, 8.
- Push the start line down: a slider from C0 (today: bought actuators, screws and electronics plus printed parts) to C4 (mining). Chips always bought.
- Materials: a ferrite Halbach ring next to a magnet-free switched reluctance motor.
- How it ships: a robot plus a kit box, then at home it builds the second.
- Size steps: 1x, 1/2x, 1/4x and 1/8x robots, each reaching over to the next smaller one.
- The penny that doubles (dark section): 33 doublings take one robot to 8.6 billion. A slider sets the weeks per generation and shows the years, e.g. 8 weeks gives 5.1 years.

Scope: the wording is short marketing copy taken from the plan. I didn't add any new claims. The penny line ($5.4M after 30 days) and 2^33 = 8.6 billion are plain arithmetic. The years figure assumes every robot builds one copy per generation and nothing runs out, which the plan doesn't claim. I checked it at desktop width. Phone-width CSS is in, but I only spot-checked it in headless Chrome.

summary: Jake wants a clean, modern single-page local website mock-up of the self-building robot plan, with many original illustrations of the two-armed legless robot, pliers gripper, sibling assembly, replication ladder and doubling curve. It should be served on localhost with a URL and start command, and a screenshot attached so he can see it without opening anything.
